model: TempTrac water heater electronic controller (Modbus RTU)
applies_to: PVI TempTrac thermostatic controllers (firmware 0.3 and 0.5) on RS-485 Modbus RTU, per PVI manual PV500-42 (06/2014).
summary: TempTrac is PVI's electronic operating control for its water heaters. It is a Modbus RTU slave on 2-wire RS-485 at a fixed 9600 8N1 and uses only holding registers (FC03/06/16, up to 5 registers per request). This map covers the registers PVI lists for typical BMS use: probe temperatures, set point, modulation rate, burner hours, relay status, alarms and the on/off command.

addressing.note: The manual uses register numbers: holding register 40001 is address 0 on the wire, so subtract 40001 (40769 -> 768). Coils are numbered from 00001 the same way, so coil 513 is wire address 512.

source.title: MODBUS-RTU Applied to the TempTrac Control
source.pages: p. 4 (register numbering), pp. 10-14 (Table 2), pp. 15-16 (typical parameters, port setup)

notes: PVI does not host this manual publicly that we could find; this copy is served by a controls distributor and is the unaltered PVI document (PVI Industries footer, document number on every page).
Only the registers in section 4.2 'Typical parameters' and the clearly readable status/alarm rows are included; the long parameter list in Table 2 (pp. 10-14) did not extract cleanly and is left out.
Temperatures are whole degrees F per section 4.2. The display resolution option (rES) applies only to Celsius; its effect on Modbus values is not documented, so Celsius operation is not covered here.

Alarm bits follow the decimal values and bit numbers in the manual (bit 0 = 1). The manual's hex values for Alarm 2 (0x1000) and Alarm 3 (0x0800) disagree with their decimal values (2048, 4096); the decimal/bit numbers are used.
Register 41281 also accepts keypad lock/unlock and buzzer-silence codes; PVI notes that only the on/off command is normally needed.
Table 2 gives a hex base-0 address next to each register number (e.g. St1 0x300 = 40769), which confirms the 40001 = address 0 rule.

registers.name: Probe 1 temperature (TP1)
registers.description: Operating probe that set point St1 controls to; degrees F.

registers.name: Probe 2 temperature (TP2)
registers.description: Returns an exception if probe 2 is disabled.

registers.name: Probe 3 temperature (TP3)
registers.description: Returns an exception if probe 3 is disabled.

registers.name: Modulation rate output
registers.description: Firmware 0.5 only: 4-20 mA modulation output, 0-100 % (0 = low fire on most units).

registers.name: Working hours relay 1 (ou1)
registers.description: Burner run hours, rolls over at 9999.

registers.name: Control command (on/off)
registers.description: Write-only command word; 257 = ON, 1 = OFF. Reads are invalid.

registers.name: Relay status
registers.description: Relay 1 bit = call for heat (burner on).

registers.name: Alarm register
registers.description: Bit meanings listed are the firmware 0.5 rows; on firmware 0.3, bit 12 flags input 2/3 alarms.

integration.summary: Poll 9600 8N1 with FC03, no more than 5 registers per request. Read probe 1 (40257), relay status (42050) and alarms (43329); write the set point at 40769 and turn the heater on/off by writing 257/1 to 41281.
integration.enable: Modbus RTU is available through the XJ485 serial interface (TTL to RS-485) connected to the TempTrac's programming port.
quirks: Maximum 5 registers per read or write.
41281 is write-only; reading it returns invalid data.
setup: Fixed serial settings: 9600 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit (not adjustable).
Set the slave address (1-247) on the keypad; each unit on the bus needs its own address.
Leave at least 500 ms before a retry. The controller has no bias resistors; bias the line at the master.
gotchas: Reading probe 2 or 3 returns an exception when that probe is disabled.
In OFF the display shows OFF and outputs are open, but temperatures can still be read.

address_note: address = 0-based Modbus wire (PDU) address; documented = as printed in the source.
note: Re-typed from the manufacturer's public documentation (see source) and verified against it. Registers vary by firmware and options; verify against the live device before writing.
